title: preview-stack-driven, plan-only Terraform canary for control-plane minor upgrades with OPA policy gates
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: implement a safe, automated path for minor control-plane version upgrades on Private (VPC) deployments using Terraform-first preview stacks and policy-as-code gates. The workflow avoids any immediate production writes until the preview stack passes a battery of compatibility, performance, and security checks. Key design principles: (1) irreversibility minimization — prefer reversible DB migrations and feature flags; (2) test-before-apply — terraform plan --> preview stack --> automated test suite --> promote; (3) policy enforcement — OPA checks for API compatibility, RBAC drift, and KMS key policies; (4) observability-driven promotion — promote only when SLO gates meet thresholds for 24h under synthetic and low-volume real traffic; (5) minimal blast radius — start with plan-only preview + 1% mirrored control-plane API sampling via VPC mirroring and a short-lived ingress adaptor.

High-level flow:
- Step A: Terraform plan pipeline creates a preview-stack using existing IaC modules but with isolated suffixes (preview-<build>) using the same VPC resources (shared subnets, isolated ENIs) and the same remote state backend with a preview lock key.
- Step B: Apply preview stack in a separate tenant-scoped path; secrets fetched using a temp KMS alias; DB replicas pushed into read-only mode for migration dry-run where applicable.
- Step C: Run automated compatibility suite: api-schema regression tests, operator-runner smoke tests, KV cache warmup profile, and quantized performance probe (50-512 token traces to exercise attention kernels).
- Step D: OPA policies evaluate plan and runtime signals (RBAC diffs, security groups, KMS policy changes, circuit-breaker config deltas). Any policy failure blocks promotion and opens a review ticket.
- Step E: Canary promotion staged via control-plane feature flags: enable new control-plane for 0.5% of mirror-sampled requests for 12 hours, then 2%, 5% etc. Promotion only proceeds if SLO gates (p95 latency, error-rate, KV-miss-rate, and unit-cost delta) remain within thresholds.
- Step F: Rollback is an automated apply of the previous stable module revision (terraform state rebind and resource replace where necessary) and immediate activation of a short-circuit fallback route in the router plane.

Terraform/IaC specifics:
- Introduce preview-stack module wrappers that parameterize state key suffixes and KMS aliasing.
- Add a plan-only CI job that stores the plan artifact in the release bucket and attaches a plan-hash to the preview stack for traceability.
- Remote state: S3 + DynamoDB locking with additional preview isolation. State migrations must be opted-in via the preview flow.
- Use Terragrunt-style composition at the infra root for preview toggles to avoid duplicating module code.

Gating metrics (measured in preview stack and during small-sample promotion):
- p95 latency (control plane API): <= baseline + 20%
- 5xx error-rate: <= baseline + 0.1%
- KV cache miss-rate: no more than baseline + 5 percentage points
- Control-plane CPU/GPU utilization: no sustained >80% for 15m
- Cost delta per token: measured and flagged if > +30%
- Security/Audit checks: zero policy violations from OPA / static analyzers

Observability and telemetry:
- Wire preview-stack metrics to a dedicated temporary dashboard (prometheus labels: preview=true, stack_id)
- Synthetic probes: 1k request set that mirrors production prompt shapes; perf traces collected and compared with historical baselines via the console-compare tool.
- Alerting: temporary alert rules with auto-muted channels for preview-promotions; automated slack shout when thresholds are crossed.

Rollout and rollback playbook (operator-facing):
- Automatic rollback conditions: >0.1% 5xx spike sustained for 5m, p95 > baseline+50% for 10m, or OPA violation surfaced.
- Manual operator escalation: if automated rollback fails, operator runs `scripts/controlplane-fallback.sh <stack-id>` to rebind routing and flip feature flag.
- Post-mortem steps: collect traces, attach plan artifact and OPA evaluation logs to the incident ticket.

Security and compliance considerations:
- Preview stack uses temporary KMS alias with restricted principals; permanent KMS rotations must be scheduled before production promotion.
- State file ACLs audited; ensure no preview artifacts retain customer data beyond retention window (7 days by default).

Success criteria:
- Automated preview job creates and verifies a preview stack for 90% of upgrade attempts without manual intervention.
- 95% of minor-version upgrade promotions can be completed using the preview-first flow with rollback automation.
- Upgrade-related incidents reduced by 60% quarter-over-quarter for Private deployments.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Whether preview stacks should be created in the same AWS account vs a mirrored account for stricter isolation (cost vs fidelity trade-off).
- How aggressively to mirror real traffic for the first promotion step (0.5% vs 1%); current lean is 0.5% to reduce blast radius.
- Whether to allow stateful DB migrations in the preview flow or require a manual opt-in migration window.

Deliverables:
- terraform module: preview-stack-wrapper (RFC + implementation)
- CI pipelines: plan-only job, preview-apply job, promotion job
- OPA policy pack for control-plane compatibility
- Console dashboards and temporary preview alerting rules
- Operator runbook and emergency rollback scripts
comments: 2025-02-12: Kickoff with infra and runtime teams. Agreed on preview stack approach and plan-only artifact retention = 7d. Action: infra to prototype preview wrapper module. -- Maya
2025-02-18: PR opened - https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-ops/pull/4123 (preview-wrapper module). Initial review from Diego: request to add explicit S3 lifecycle rules for preview plans.
2025-02-24: OPA policy draft v0.1 uploaded to repo - https://github.com/redwood-inference/policies/tree/main/controlplane. Request from security: add KMS principal enumeration check. -- Lars

2025-02-28: Integration run completed in staging account (preview-20250228-01). Synthetic probe results: p95 +8%, KV miss-rate +2%. No OPA violations. Moving to small-sample mirrored promotion (0.5%) later this week.

2025-03-03: First micro-canary promotion observed a 0.06% increase in 5xx for 4m then recovered. Automated rollback triggered and succeeded. Root cause: short-lived cache warmup causing transient spikes. Mitigation: introduce warmup step to pre-warm caches before promotion. -- Lars
Next steps: finish PR comments, add S3 lifecycle rule, finalize OPA checks for KMS, and schedule a dry-run promotion for the next maintenance window (2025-03-12).
